intro: A full review of Pladids — Chon Buri's Bib Gourmand pick — with everything you need to know before you go: price, booking/queue tips, must-order dishes, and how to get there
quickAnswerHtml: Pladids is a Bib Gourmand restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, in Chon Buri, in Tambon Pong, Bang Lamung (east Pattaya). Budget around THB 500–1,000, and you can book ahead

blocks.html:
Say "Pattaya" and the first image that comes to mind is probably the walking street, beachfront seafood buffets, and big restaurants seating a hundred tourists at once. Pladids is the opposite of all of that. It's tucked away in Tambon Pong, Bang Lamung, on the east Pattaya side that tourists almost never drive through — a tiny chef's-table restaurant seating only about 2 tables a day. What really makes people's eyes widen is that there's no fixed menu at all, not even one dish — the chef cooks whatever the small local fishing boats bring in that day. Whatever fish the boats come back with, that's what you eat. It's a kind of honesty that's hard to find in a tourist town this size, and Michelin agrees, awarding it a new Bib Gourmand in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, praising the "complex yet balanced" flavours of the seasonal set served alongside jasmine rice.

The word "set" is the heart of the place. You don't order dish by dish — instead the chef puts together a full set menu for the meal, which rotates with the seasons and whatever the sea provides that day. The dishes people talk about most often include Thai fish sashimi — yes, fish from our own gulf, sliced and served raw, proof that truly fresh local fish can be every bit as good raw as anything else — and salt-boiled squid, a dish so simple it's almost hard to believe it's a standout, but that simplicity is sharpest when the ingredients are genuinely fresh off the boat. The budget isn't as steep as you'd think either, at around THB 500–1,000 per person — great value for a chef's-table experience this close, built around seasonal seafood sets.

One thing worth knowing before you go: the Bang Lamung side of Chon Buri still has real small-boat fishing communities that go out day by day, and Pladids is the restaurant that puts that way of life straight onto the table — no central market, no cold storage in between. That's exactly why the restaurant can only take so few guests and why bookings fill up a month or more in advance — there's only ever as much as the sea gives that day. If you're tired of the bucket-seafood image along Pattaya's beachfront and want to know what real eastern Thai seafood tastes like, this is the answer — just plan ahead.

blocks.name: Pladids
blocks.descHtml:
Pladids takes bookings in advance only — no walk-ins, ever. It's open for two dinner sittings only: 17:00–18:30 and 19:00–20:30, seating roughly 2 tables per sitting per day. To book, follow the restaurant's Facebook page (facebook.com/pladids.mp), which announces booking windows periodically, or call 084-455-6145 — the queue fills up fast, and most people need to book a month or more ahead. If you're planning a Pattaya trip, book this before you even book your hotel. The seasonal set runs around THB 500–1,000 per person (Wongnai lists it as THB 501–1,000), and the dress code is casual.

The restaurant is in Tambon Pong, Bang Lamung, on the east Pattaya side, a fair distance from the beach zone and the walking street, with no public transport passing by — you'll need to drive or grab a ride. It's worth pinning the exact coordinates from the restaurant's page before you set off, allowing about 20–30 minutes from central Pattaya, and aim to arrive 10–15 minutes before your sitting, since each sitting runs exactly an hour and a half. There's no menu to choose from — the chef builds the set from whatever the small fishing boats bring in that day, so flag any seafood allergies when you book.
